title: Grade 4 Science — Thu, Jun 26
description: Food and Digestion — Day 4 of 5: Balanced diet and nutrients
subject: science

questions.question: A balanced diet contains all nutrients in the right amounts. Which group below lists the FIVE main nutrients?
questions.explanation: The five major nutrient groups: Carbohydrates (energy), Proteins (growth/repair), Fats (energy/insulation), Vitamins (disease prevention), Minerals (body functions). Plus water and fibre — often counted as essential dietary components.

questions.question: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates (starch, sugar) are broken down to glucose — the body's primary fuel. Rice, roti, bread, potatoes are rich carbohydrate sources.

questions.question: Proteins are needed for:
options: Growth, repair of body tissues and building muscles
questions.explanation: Proteins are the body's 'building blocks' — used for growth (making new cells), repair of damaged tissues, and building enzymes, hormones and antibodies. Sources: dal, eggs, meat, fish, milk, cheese.

questions.question: Which food is the RICHEST source of protein?
questions.explanation: Dal (lentils) and eggs are excellent protein sources. Animal proteins (eggs, meat, fish) are 'complete' proteins (contain all essential amino acids). Lentils are a rich plant-based source — important for vegetarian diets.

questions.question: Vitamins are needed in small amounts but are essential. Vitamin C deficiency causes:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency → scurvy (bleeding gums, slow wound healing, poor immunity). Found in citrus fruits (oranges, lemons), amla (Indian gooseberry). Indian context: amla is one of the richest sources of vitamin C.

questions.question: Calcium is a mineral needed for:
questions.explanation: Calcium builds and maintains strong bones and teeth. Deficiency → weak bones (osteoporosis in adults, rickets in children). Sources: milk, cheese, paneer, yogurt, ragi, sesame seeds.

questions.question: Fats provide energy and help absorb certain vitamins (A, D, E, K). Which statement is TRUE about fats?
options: A small amount of fat is essential for health — fat-soluble vitamins cannot be absorbed without fat; excess fat is stored for energy
Fat and carbohydrates are the same nutrient
questions.explanation: Fats ARE necessary — they carry fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), provide concentrated energy (9 kcal/g vs 4 for carbs), insulate the body, protect organs. EXCESS fat leads to obesity; too little also harms health.

questions.question: Iron is a mineral found in spinach, dates, meat and beans. What does iron do in the body?
options: Is a component of haemoglobin in red blood cells — carries oxygen throughout the body
questions.explanation: Iron is essential for haemoglobin (the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen). Iron deficiency → anaemia (fatigue, pale skin, weakness). Spinach, pomegranate, dates are iron-rich Indian foods.

questions.question: A child eats only rice and bread every day and avoids vegetables, dal and fruits. What is MOST likely to happen?
options: The child will be very healthy
The child will get enough energy but suffer nutrient deficiencies (vitamins, minerals, protein) — leading to poor growth, weak immunity and possible deficiency diseases
The child will grow very tall
The child will have too many vitamins
questions.explanation: Rice and bread provide carbohydrates (energy) but lack protein, vitamins and minerals. Without these, the child faces: slow growth (protein deficiency), weak bones (calcium), anaemia (iron), poor immunity (vitamins). This is malnutrition.

questions.question: Vitamin D is sometimes called the 'sunshine vitamin.' Why?
options: It makes skin look sunny and yellow
The skin produces Vitamin D when exposed to sunlight — making outdoor activity essential for bone health
It is found only in summer fruits
questions.explanation: Sunlight triggers the skin to synthesise Vitamin D. Vitamin D helps absorb calcium → builds strong bones. Deficiency → rickets in children (soft, bowed legs). In India, deficiency is surprisingly common despite abundant sunshine.

questions.question: What is the difference between MACRONUTRIENTS and MICRONUTRIENTS?
options: Macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats) are needed in large amounts for energy and structure; micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) are needed in tiny amounts but are equally essential for body functions
Micronutrients provide most of the body's energy
questions.explanation: Macro = large: carbs, proteins, fats — body needs grams per day for energy and building. Micro = tiny: vitamins (milligrams/micrograms), minerals (milligrams) — tiny amounts but critical for chemical reactions and processes.

questions.question: Roughage (dietary fibre) is found in vegetables, fruits and whole grains. It is NOT digested. Why is it still essential?
options: It adds bulk to food, stimulates peristalsis (gut movements), prevents constipation, and feeds beneficial gut bacteria
questions.explanation: Fibre passes through undigested but is vital: (1) prevents constipation by adding bulk, (2) feeds good gut bacteria (prebiotics), (3) slows sugar absorption (good for blood sugar control). Essential for a healthy digestive system.

questions.question: A traditional Indian thali (meal) often has: roti/rice + dal + sabzi + curd + salad. Why is this meal considered balanced?
options: It is not balanced at all
Roti/rice = carbohydrates; dal = protein; sabzi = vitamins/minerals; curd = protein+calcium; salad = fibre — together they cover all five nutrient groups
questions.explanation: A well-planned Indian thali is nutritionally balanced: grain (carbs+fibre) + legume (protein) + cooked vegetable (vitamins+minerals) + dairy (protein+calcium+fat) + raw salad (fibre+vitamins) = all five nutrient categories covered.

questions.question: Why do growing children need MORE protein per kilogram of body weight than adults?
options: Children are smaller so they need more
Children are actively building NEW tissues (muscle, organ growth) whereas adults mainly need protein for maintenance and repair
questions.explanation: Growing children use protein to build new muscle, bones, enzymes and organs — not just to maintain existing ones. This high rate of tissue formation demands more protein relative to body weight than maintenance needs of adults.

questions.question: Iodine is a mineral needed for thyroid gland function. What food source is iodine commonly added to in India?
questions.explanation: Iodised salt has iodine added to prevent goitre (enlarged thyroid) — a public health measure. Iodine deficiency is common in hilly/inland areas without access to seafood. Using iodised salt is a simple, effective solution.
